researchers: people who carry out careful study
Researchers have tracked the glacier's retreat for thirty years.
film: The film won several awards at the festival.
colossal: extremely large in size or extent

squid: a sea creature with a long soft body and several arms

in: expressing location inside or within something

its: belonging to a thing, animal, or situation already mentioned

natural: existing in or produced by nature; not artificial

habitat: the natural home of an animal or plant
Logging destroyed much of the bird's original habitat.
for: intended to belong to, or be given to, someone or something

the: used before a noun to refer to a specific or already-known thing

first: coming before all others in order or time

time: the continuous progress of existence measured in seconds, minutes, hours, etc.

remotely: from a distance, without being physically present

operated: worked or functioned, or was controlled and run by someone

vehicle: a machine used for transporting people or goods

on: positioned at or touching the surface of something

an: used before a word starting with a vowel sound to mean 'one'

ocean: a very large area of sea

census: an official count or survey of a population

expedition: a journey made for a particular purpose, such as exploration

has: has; present tense of have, third person singular

filmed: The documentary filmed rare footage of wolves hunting at night.
young: having lived or existed for only a short time

deep: positioned far down from the surface

south: the direction that is opposite to north

atlantic: the ocean lying between the Americas and Europe/Africa

confirmed: established that something is true or definitely the case

footage: recorded video material, especially of a particular event
cảnh quay, đoạn phim ghi hình

of: used to show belonging, origin, or a relationship between two things

species: a group of living things that can breed together and share characteristics

alive: Despite the harsh winter, the old tree remained alive.
wednesday: the day of the week between Tuesday and Thursday

april: the fourth month of the year

university: an institution of higher education offering degrees

essex: The university in Essex published new research on deep-sea creatures.
england: a country that is part of the United Kingdom

reported: Local media reported heavy flooding across the province.
that: used to identify a specific thing, person, or clause already mentioned

had: past tense of have, used to show possession or a completed action

recorded: written down or stored for later reference

member: a person who belongs to a group or organisation

glass: a hard, transparent material used for windows and containers

family: a group of related people, or a group of related things

living: She is one of the few living witnesses to that event.
sea: the salt water covering most of the earth's surface

sighting: an occasion of seeing something, especially something rare

30-centimeter: measuring 30 centimeters in length or size

juvenile: A juvenile eagle was spotted testing its wings near the nest.
took: past tense of take; obtained, seized, or required something

place: a particular position, location, or area
This quiet park is my favorite place to read on weekends.
march: the third month of the year

near: at a short distance from a place, time or state

uninhabited: không có người ở, hoang vắng

sandwich: two slices of bread with filling between them
She packed a cheese sandwich for lunch.
islands: plural of island: pieces of land surrounded by water

part: a piece or portion of a whole

british: relating to Britain or its people

overseas: situated in or coming from a foreign country across the sea

territory: an area of land, especially defined by ownership, control, or culture

obtained: got or acquired something, usually through effort
đã thu được, đã có được

roughly: The trip takes roughly three hours by car.
meters: units of length equal to 100 centimetres

beneath: in or to a lower position than something

surface: the outer or top layer of something

marked: labelled or indicated in a particular way

years: Somebody must own the roof and repaint it every few years.
since: from a particular time in the past until now, or because

was: past tense of 'be', used for the first/third person singular

formally: in an official or conventional manner

recognized: formally acknowledged or identified as already known

and: used to connect words, phrases, or clauses

named: given a particular name; specifically mentioned

called: named or referred to by a particular term
The recipe uses a fermented paste called miso for extra flavour.
subastian: SuBastian, a remotely operated underwater robot used for deep-sea exploration
SuBastian descended nearly 4,500 meters to film the coral reef.
captured: The documentary captured the daily struggles of rural farmers.
photographs: pictures taken with a camera, plural

video: a recording of moving images, often with sound

launched: started something, or sent a rocket or vehicle into use

from: indicating the point where something starts or originates

schmidt: part of the name Schmidt Ocean Institute, a marine research organization

institute: an organisation set up for a particular purpose, especially research or education

research: careful study to discover new facts

falkor: the name of an ocean research vessel

too: The height of the band carries information too.
it: used to refer to a thing, animal, or situation already mentioned

35-day: lasting for a period of 35 days

flagship: the most important or leading item in a group
The new store is the company's flagship location in the region.
searching: Searching for the right word can slow down a beginner writer.
new: not existing before; recently made, discovered or experienced

marine: The reserve protects a wide range of marine species.
life: the state of being alive, or the period from birth to death

according: in a way that agrees with or depends on something

to: expressing direction, purpose, or a recipient

voyage: a long journey, especially by sea or in space

aboard: on or into a ship, aircraft, or other vehicle

international: The conference attracted researchers from many international universities.
effort: physical or mental energy used to do something
Learning a new language takes years of steady effort.
discover: to find or learn something for the first time

brought: carried or took something to a place, past tense of bring

together: with each other; combined into one group or place

several: more than two but not very many

institutions: plural of institution: large, established organisations

initiatives: new plans or actions intended to solve a problem
The city launched several initiatives to reduce plastic waste.
including: containing as part of a larger group; used to give an example

project: a planned piece of work with a particular purpose

gosouth: the name of a deep-sea research expedition project
(tên riêng) dự án nghiên cứu GoSouth

with: Neighbourhoods with few trees heat up fastest, and these are often the poorest districts.
dr: abbreviation for 'doctor', used as a title
Dr. Smith will see the next patient in five minutes.
michelle: Michelle led the research team's expedition to the deep sea.
taylor: a marine scientist involved in the deep-sea expedition

leading: most important or most successful in a particular field
She works for one of the leading hospitals in the country.
scientific: relating to or based on science
The claim lacked any solid scientific evidence.
team: a group of people who work or play together
The design team met every Monday to review new ideas.
said: past tense of say; spoke or expressed something in words
She said the meeting would start at nine o'clock.
incredible: The view from the summit was simply incredible.
we: used to refer to the speaker and one or more other people

can: used to express ability or possibility

leverage: to use something to gain the greatest possible advantage
tận dụng, khai thác lợi thế

power: electricity or energy supplied to run a device

taxonomic: relating to the scientific classification of organisms

community: a group of people living in the same place or sharing something

through: moving in one side and out the other; by means of

telepresence: technology that lets someone feel present at a remote location via video or robotics
hiện diện từ xa (qua công nghệ)

while: It makes the city liveable while the wider problem is dealt with separately.
are: present tense form of 'to be' used with you, we, they

out: away from the inside of a place; not in
She stepped out for a few minutes to get some fresh air.
at: used to show a specific place, time or point

deep-sea: relating to or found in the deepest parts of the ocean

biologist: a scientist who studies living organisms
The biologist spent months tracking whales along the coast.
kat: a female given name, short for Katherine

bolstad: a surname belonging to a deep-sea biologist in the article
họ của một nhà sinh vật học

auckland: the largest city in New Zealand
The research team is based at a university in Auckland.
technology: the practical application of scientific knowledge, especially in industry

who: used to ask about or refer to a person

did: past tense of 'do', used to form questions and negatives or as a main verb

not: used to make a statement, verb, or phrase negative

take: to get hold of, remove, or carry something

helped: gave assistance to; past tense of help

identify: recognise or establish who or what something is

shown: past participle of show: made clear or demonstrated

we're: It's a recent term so we're still monitoring how it is used.
finally: after a long time or delay; at last

seeing: perceiving with the eyes; becoming aware of something

this: used to refer to a specific thing nearby or just mentioned

animal: a living creature that is not a plant, often able to move

some: an unspecified amount or number of something

us: used to refer to the speaker and others, as the object

have: used with a past participle to form perfect tenses

been: past participle of be, used to show a completed state or experience

studying: the act of spending time learning about a subject

dreaming: experiencing thoughts and images during sleep

about: The lecture was about how cities cope with extreme heat.
decades: The old bridge has stood for decades without major repairs.
